summary:
Mars EVA Command is a free, browser-based tool that turns NASA’s Mars maps into one safe Marswalk, plus the way home. Earth is up to 22 light-minutes away, so astronauts can’t count on mission control in real time. Every walk must be planned before the hatch opens.

You pick a start and destination on a Mars globe at Jezero Crater. Using NASA’s 1-metre HiRISE terrain, the app finds the shortest route under a safe slope limit. It also works out the walk home from every point and checks oxygen and daylight, then gives a clear Go / No-go. You can rehearse the walk in 3D, with real-time hazard warnings and a THEMIS thermal map.

This answers the challenge by turning scattered NASA data (HiRISE, CTX, THEMIS, Mars Trek and Perseverance’s traverse and weather) into a survival decision. On a real 6.67 km science walk, it found that 45 % lies beyond a 2 km walk-home limit. Our map also marks 99.2 % of Perseverance’s real path as passable.

It works offline and is explained in Arabic and English, so students in Palestine and beyond can use it too.
details:
Mars EVA Command turns NASA’s maps of Mars into one safe walk for an astronaut, and the way home. Earth is up to 22 light-minutes away, so the plan has to be made before the hatch opens.

How it works: you pick a start and destination on a Mars globe at Jezero Crater. The app finds the shortest walk under a slope limit on NASA’s 1 m HiRISE terrain, using A* with the cost distance × (1 + (slope/15°)²) × data-confidence penalty. It also works out the walk home from every point. It then gives oxygen, daylight and a Go / No-go, and lets you rehearse the route in 3D with real-time hazard warnings and a THEMIS thermal map.

NASA data: HiRISE, CTX, Mars Trek (MDIM 2.1, MOLA), THEMIS IRPBT2, USGS SIM 3464, Mars 2020 traverse and images, MEDA, RAD, DONKI and the Mars Climate Database.

Impact:

  • Mission planners get a checked EVA plan in minutes. We found that 45 % of a real 6.67 km science walk is beyond a 2 km walk-home limit.
  • Scientists can test options: a backup rover cuts the worst walk home from 3.46 to 1.42 km.
  • Students in Palestine can use it for free, offline, in Arabic and English.
  • Validation: 99.2 % of Perseverance’s real 17.5 km path falls on ground we mark as passable, and 82 automated tests run on every change.

Tools: Python (GDAL, NumPy, SciPy), JavaScript and Three.js, an offline web app (service worker), GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. No special hardware.

Creativity: other tools show data layers; we turn them into a single survival decision you can rehearse like a game. Every value says whether it comes from an observation, a rover measurement, a model or an assumption. We considered communication delay, slope limits from Moon walks, data confidence, oxygen, daylight, accessibility and our limits honestly: this is a planning aid, not a certified safety system.

AI disclosure: drafted with an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic), then reviewed and tested by the team.

Links: https://aboodbasill.github.io/mars-eva-command/ · https://github.com/aboodbasill/mars-eva-command
